item.title: 5 Forgotten Single-Player FPS Games That Aged Like Fine Wine
item.description:
Single-player FPS games aren't as common as they used to be, at least when it comes to AAA releases. We might get 3 or 4 big titles per year, and they tend to be either multiplayer-only or feature a single-player campaign that barely lasts 5 hours. I miss the days when publishers would drop experimental mid-tier shooters like Jurassic: The Hunted , The Conduit , Dreamkiller , and NecroVisioN , all of which came out in 2009.

While indie developers have picked up the slack and can keep most people busy, there is also the option to check out some forgotten FPS games from yesteryear, quite a few of which have aged well. The genre established its core mechanics in the early 2000s, and things haven't changed that much since then; consequently, a 2010 shooter can feel just as good as a 2025 successor.

Call of Juarez: Gunslinger Is A Spaghetti Western Blast

Perfect Blend Of Style, Gameplay, And Story

  • Stylized visuals have stood the test of time.
  • The western setting still feels fresh.
  • Just cool.

Call of Juarez doesn't get enough love in general, and part of that might have to do with the series wrecking its momentum with The Cartel . After that misguided attempt to jump forward to the modern day, Techland and Ubisoft wisely opted to return to Call of Juarez 's roots with Gunslinger ​​​​​, although a digital-only release suggested a lack of confidence in its potential.

In a sea of brown and grey shooters, Gunslinger 's colorful comic book-style visuals, Wild West setting, myth-based storytelling, and short-burst arcade gameplay let it float to the top; in fact, this combination is still unusual today, especially for an AA game by a major publisher. Blending history and fiction, the campaign casts you as Silas Greaves as he recounts his tales of misadventures as a bounty hunter, including run-ins with the likes of Billy the Kid and Butch Cassidy.

10 Best AA First-Person Shooter Games, Officially Ranked

Plenty of AA FPS games fly under the radar all the time for not reaching the AAA status. Here are some of the best ones in this category.

By Mark Sammut

The framing device influences the mission's presentation, with Silas occasionally changing the story and causing the world to morph around him. Although not the snappiest gunplay ever, Gunslinger still feels good to control, especially its Concentration system that lets you slow down time and snap off multiple shots at once. Showdowns are also a blast.

Gunslinger is perpetually on sale on the Nintendo Switch , and I really recommend picking it up.

Peter Jackson's King Kong Is The Perfect Movie Adaptation

Don't Be Scared By The Licensed Game Curse

  • Immersive presentation with no HUD.
  • Multiple gameplay styles.
  • Incredibly ambitious for a licensed game from this era.

I will never miss an opportunity to discuss Peter Jackson's King Kong , just to keep its name alive, considering it has been delisted for more than a decade now. During the 2000s, few phrases sparked trepidation quite like "movie tie-in game," and hoping for anything better than a rushed mess was a recipe for disappointment. King Kong might be lumped in with other failures of the era, but it doesn't deserve to be mentioned alongside the likes of Sega's Marvel games, Fight Club , or Catwoman .

Once you get into gameplay, you will instantly realize that King Kong is something special . Why? Well, you won't see a health bar, an ammo counter, or a traditional crosshair. Instead, you rely on sensory cues to figure out this crucial information , a decision that instantly showed that Ubisoft sought to create an immersive experience rather than just Turok with King Kong (as awesome as that sounds). You don't feel like an action hero, and you certainly don't become Rambo running through a forest and killing everything that moves.

The wildlife AI was fantastic for its era and still holds up pretty well. As ammo is scarce, the game encourages players to think outside the box and manipulate their environment to get past predators, including using weaker animals as distractions. Humans are weak, so they need to be smart.

Oh, right, you also play as Kong. It is as empowering as it sounds.

Project Snowblind Is Linear Deus Ex (And That's A Good Thing)

Slow Down Time, Throw A Grenade, And Blow Up A Tank

  • Augmented gunplay and the many ways you can destroy enemies.
  • A fast-paced linear shooter.

A Deux Ex game that ended up becoming something else entirely, Project Snowblind shows its lineage through its augmentations, top-notch gunplay, and sheer power fantasy factor. Dropping any immersive-sim elements in favor of linear arcade gunplay, Crystal Dynamics' game has aged better than any of the older Deus Ex games, even though the original is still far more impressive today.

While you might be mostly walking down a straight path, Project Snowblind offers freedom through the techniques and abilities available to players. "Reflext Boost" lets you slow down time, while Cloak lets you go invisible, and the fun comes from figuring out ways to smartly implement them during missions. The weapon selection is also quite robust, even including an Icepick gun that takes control of electronics such as mechs or turrets.

Project Snowblind certainly looks its age, more so than any other game in this article. However, the combat still feels surprisingly smooth.

​​​​​​​Hard Reset Set The Stage For Modern FPS Games

The Boomer Shooter Before Boomer Shooters

  • One of the last true AA FPS games.
  • Available in an improved form ( Hard Reset Redux )

I struggled to decide whether Hard Reset qualifies as forgotten, since I always come across the game when searching through stores for shooters. Ultimately, Flying Wild Hog's first game doesn't have the same cult following as its more celebrated peers, especially Bulletstorm and Shadow Warrior , and the Redux version doesn't even have 2K reviews on Steam despite releasing more than a decade ago.

Hard Reset is the missing link between classic '90s shooters and modern boomer shooters, occupying that AA space that is almost entirely extinct today. In 2011, an uncompromising PC-first FPS game that emphasized fast movement, weapon-mode management, and raw aim was far removed from the genre's typical releases, even if it was a touch rough around the edges in places. Even its neon lighting and sci-fi weapons set it apart from the military crowd.

The Hardest FPS Games Ever Made, Ranked

First-person shooters are a tough genre to get into if someone has never played them before. Some get so hard that they are nearly impossible.

By Charles Burgar

Moving away from the "select two weapons" loadouts, Hard Reset 's best feature is that it offers only two weapons with multiple configurations that can be swapped on the fly. Your standard assault rifle physically shifts and reassembles itself on the fly into a shotgun, a grenade launcher, a rocket launcher, or a proximity mine layer.

Dark Messiah of Might and Magic Set An Unbeatable Bar For FPS RPGs

The Perfect Combat

  • Physics-based combat is top-notch.
  • A proper sandbox that encourages experimentation.

Does this count? Dark Messiah of Might and Magic is first-and-foremost an action RPG, but it also plays like a first-person shooter with magic and a sword (and a bow). Two decades later, Dark Messiah 's genre combination continues to be extremely rare, and part of that might be due to the fact that Arkane kind of nailed the first-person combat immediately.

Because Arkane built the game on Valve’s Source Engine, the entire world is incredibly tactile, reactive, and physically modeled. If you try to play it like a traditional first-person hack and slash, Dark Messiah punishes you significantly, as you are meant to treat the environment as your primary weapon. Well, that and your boot, as kicking goblins off scaffolds is simply the best.

Magic can be fired essentially like a gun, but it's most effective when used to exploit the physics, such as freezing a stone floor to make guards slip. The combat is just so eternally fun.

8 Near-Perfect FPS Games That Are Certified Flops

A first-person shooter can do everything right and still fail to meet commercial expectations. This FPS games didn't find a big enough audience.

2
By Ollie Tuscarny

item.title: How to Get Dandilord in Palworld 1.0
item.description:
With more than 180 Pals available in Palworld 1.0 , finding a specific one can take far longer than expected, especially when certain species only appear in progression-locked areas. Dandilord is one of those elusive Pals, making it well worth knowing exactly where to search before heading out. Plus, it has the highest Planting Work suitability in the game, making it essential for late-game crop management.

Whether you're looking to complete your Paldeck, strengthen your combat team, or take advantage of Dandilord's unique abilities, tracking it down is the first step. This guide explains how to get Dandilord in Palworld 1.0 , including where to find it, the best way to catch it, and alternative methods for obtaining it.

Best Pals for Combat in Palworld 1.0

Discover the most powerful Pals for combat in Palworld 1.0, ranked by effectiveness, damage potential, and versatility.

By Lucas Simons

Dandilord Location in Palworld 1.0

Dandilord is one of the newest pals added with Palworld 1.0, and to find it, players need to visit the legendary World Tree region, which is only accessible after finding and defeating Panthalus.

After entering the World Tree region, head northeast, past the Dusty Ravine Watchtower , and look further north for the Rootmist Root zone. Descend the ravine to find a mysterious altar shining with a purple Light and a Teleporter.

This is the zone where you can start the Dandilord Boss Fight , which will be conducted in a separate instance. Make sure you bring at least a Sol Sphere to Catch Dandilord after beating it.

Bringing Pals who deal Mercy hits or carrying the Mercy Ring yourself will help to avoid dealing lethal damage to Dandilord. After reducing it to 1 HP, throw the Pal Sphere to nail the catch.

How To Get Shaolong In Palworld

Here's where to find the mighty Shaolong and how to catch it in Palworld.

By Nahda Nabiilah

Dandilord has the highest planting suitability of all Pals (Lv. 8), but it also has Handiwork Lv. 6, Gathering Lv. 5, Medicine Production Lv. 6, and Transporting Lv. 3. Its ground speed is also incredibly high (over 800), making it one of the fastest bipedal Pals in the Paldeck.

This comes with a catch, though: it consumes a ridiculous amount of Food, and its sanity bar doesn't last long. Make sure to have a suitable Pal Bed for it, and an Alpha Wave Emitter installed in the base to make sure its sanity doesn't drop faster.

You can also build a High-Quality Hot Spring or a Japanese-style Hot Spring to allow Dandilord to relax between its frantic Planting and Harvesting cycles.

What's That Weapon?

Identify the silhouettes before time runs out.

How to Breed Dandilord in Palworld 1.0

Contrary to what many say, Dandilord is one of those Pals that can only be obtained by breeding two Dandilords. That doesn't mean that breeding Dandilord is useless.

On the contrary, using Dandilord to breed might result in some incredibly rare Pals. Here's a complete breeding chart for Dandilord in Palworld:

  • Dandilord + Azurobe = Venusa
  • Dandilord + Mozzarina = Skutlass
  • Dandilord + Kelpsea = Shroomer Noct
  • Dandilord + Kelpsea Ignis = Icelyn
  • Dandilord + Anubis = Knocklem
  • Dandilord + Arsox = Bulldosu
  • Dandilord + Astegon = Solenne
  • Dandilord + Azurmane = Ophydia
  • Dandilord + Beakon = Sekhmet
  • Dandilord + Bastigor = Aegidron
  • Dandilord + Jetragon = Aegidron
  • Dandilord + Jormuntide = Eidrolon
  • Dandilord + Jormuntide Ignis = Aegidron
  • Dandilord + Bellanoir = Eidrolon
  • Dandilord + Broncherry Aqua = Silvegis
  • Dandilord + Elphidran = Gildra
  • Dandilord + Tetroise Primo = Ophydia
  • Dandilord + Xenogard = Duplin
  • Dandilord + Caprity Noct = Majex
  • Dandilord + Direhowl = Solmora
  • Dandilord + Whalasca = Flaracle
  • Dandilord + Carnibora = Ghangler
  • Dandilord + Majex = Roujay
  • Dandilord + Dandilord = Dandilord

From all of those combinations, crossing it with Elphidran to get a Gildra (which has a powerful resurrection skill), and with Carnibora to get a Ghangler (best pal for Fishing) should be your top priority. With more than 180 Pals available in Palworld 1.0 , finding a specific one can take far longer than expected, especially when certain species only appear in progression-locked areas. Dandilord is one of those elusive Pals, making it well worth knowing exactly where to search before heading out. Plus, it has the highest Planting Work suitability in the game, making it essential for late-game crop management.

Whether you're looking to complete your Paldeck, strengthen your combat team, or take advantage of Dandilord's unique abilities, tracking it down is the first step. This guide explains how to get Dandilord in Palworld 1.0 , including where to find it, the best way to catch it, and alternative methods for obtaining it.

Best Pals for Combat in Palworld 1.0

Discover the most powerful Pals for combat in Palworld 1.0, ranked by effectiveness, damage potential, and versatility.

By Lucas Simons

Dandilord Location in Palworld 1.0

Dandilord is one of the newest pals added with Palworld 1.0, and to find it, players need to visit the legendary World Tree region, which is only accessible after finding and defeating Panthalus.

After entering the World Tree region, head northeast, past the Dusty Ravine Watchtower , and look further north for the Rootmist Root zone. Descend the ravine to find a mysterious altar shining with a purple Light and a Teleporter.

This is the zone where you can start the Dandilord Boss Fight , which will be conducted in a separate instance. Make sure you bring at least a Sol Sphere to Catch Dandilord after beating it.

Bringing Pals who deal Mercy hits or carrying the Mercy Ring yourself will help to avoid dealing lethal damage to Dandilord. After reducing it to 1 HP, throw the Pal Sphere to nail the catch.

How To Get Shaolong In Palworld

Here's where to find the mighty Shaolong and how to catch it in Palworld.

By Nahda Nabiilah

Dandilord has the highest planting suitability of all Pals (Lv. 8), but it also has Handiwork Lv. 6, Gathering Lv. 5, Medicine Production Lv. 6, and Transporting Lv. 3. Its ground speed is also incredibly high (over 800), making it one of the fastest bipedal Pals in the Paldeck.

This comes with a catch, though: it consumes a ridiculous amount of Food, and its sanity bar doesn't last long. Make sure to have a suitable Pal Bed for it, and an Alpha Wave Emitter installed in the base to make sure its sanity doesn't drop faster.

You can also build a High-Quality Hot Spring or a Japanese-style Hot Spring to allow Dandilord to relax between its frantic Planting and Harvesting cycles.

item.title: How to Solve the Numbers and Shapes Puzzle in The Mermaid Mask (Mess Hall)
item.description:
While you're exploring the rather large submarine in The Mermaid Mask , you can interact with a big metal statue of a serpent in the Mess Hall room. You can choose to peer in and look closer at the cabinet that's built into the structure, leading you into the first major puzzle for the detective game that involves four numbered rotating dials with shapes inside of them.

Here's how to solve the shapes and numbers puzzle in The Mermaid Mask .

Solution to the Shapes and Numbers Puzzle in The Mermaid Mask (Mess Hall Guide)

The shapes and numbers puzzle in The Mermaid Mask might appear confusing at first, but the solution is rather simple: the numbers on each window need to match the number of sides on each shape in each respective window.

  • So, for the first window on the left with the number 3, you just need one shape with three sides, which is the blue triangle.
  • For the second window with the number 9, you'll need to put the orange square and the yellow pentagon (four sides plus five sides equals 9!).
  • The number 7 window needs the orange square and blue triangle.
  • The number 4 window just needs the orange square.

Just rotate the dials until everything is in the right spot, then click the keyhole button in the top-right corner to complete the puzzle and move on with the deadly investigation.

Death Note: 10 Anime Detectives Who Would Have Caught Light Before L

L is one of anime's most celebrated detectives, but the best detectives in anime history could have caught Kira much sooner.

By Rodrigo Sandoval Lahut
